observation_summary: The NumericEntityUnescaper throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when processing strings that end abruptly without a semicolon, because it attempts to access characters beyond the string length.
reasoning_summary: The root cause is a missing boundary check in the while loop (line 54) of NumericEntityUnescaper.java. The code assumes that a semicolon will always be found within the string bounds, but it fails to validate if the 'end' index has reached the end of the input string before calling charAt(end). This is a classic missing guard/boundary check.
evidence_used: Stack trace: java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: String index out of range

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop logic is flawed, the primary failure is the lack of a boundary check (guard) to prevent the index from exceeding the string length, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
